```
$ rclone-v1.52.0 size --drive-root-folder-id "1vbyJ26ojnw5NvEpL2mrRkl5N--zqc1yZ" TestDrive:

```
$ rclone-v1.52.0 --disable ListR size --drive-root-folder-id "1vbyJ26ojnw5NvEpL2mrRkl5N--zqc1yZ" TestDrive:
Total objects: 354
Total size: 2.853 GBytes (3063873067 Bytes)
```

This sounds very similar to #4018 which was fixed with 38e59ebdf30482ca9fa2b850e6f65aa065634a67

Looking at the diff of the file listings it appears to have a similar cause - namely it isn't recursing in to the directories when it should.

I will investigate further...

This is potentially related to this issue: https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/3114

since the folder is publically available , it definitely isnt a team drive , its just a public folder from someone else's google account . This issue can also be reproduced in _Shared with me_ remote ( wherein the root folder id in config is that of a google drive folder is only accessible by you , ie only privately shared ones  )

These queries work fine normally if done one ID at a time (eg when you `--disable ListR`).

I tried these queries in the [API explorer](https://developers.google.com/drive/api/v3/reference/files/list?apix_params=%7B%22includeItemsFromAllDrives%22%3Atrue%2C%22includeTeamDriveItems%22%3Atrue%2C%22q%22%3A%22((%271nJBJzllQF63jA2kMPwkwtCTUV7PD_tkR%27%20in%20parents)%20or%20(%271yIWAJcjkUOhppRy2Tppw1wFO-nqEDFX7%27%20in%20parents))%22%2C%22supportsAllDrives%22%3Atrue%2C%22supportsTeamDrives%22%3Afalse%7D) with the same result..

I'm thinking that this is a bug in Google Drive unless we can think of some query parameter I've missed

It looks like a bug has been reported about this or something very similar

https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/149522397

I think rclone needs to engage a work-around for this....

Note that we can detect the problem like this...

If we get an empty listing when querying for multiple parents:
- try querying each directory individually
- if any of them return things set the workaround flag to no longer do multiple directory queries

This will potentially be inefficient if there are a lot of empty directories, however I don't think that is very common.

I had a go at making a workaround here - can you have a test?

https://beta.rclone.org/branch/v1.52.0-004-g96c6137c-fix-4289-listr-shared-beta/ (uploaded in 15-30 mins)

    drive: fix missing items when listing using --fast-list / ListR
    
    This is caused by a bug in Google drive where, in some circumstances
    querying for "(A in parents) or (B in parents)" returns nothing
    whereas querying for "A in parents" and "B in parents" separately
    works fine.
    
    This has been reported here:
    
    https://issuetracker.google.com/issues/149522397
    
    This workaround detects this condition by seeing if a listing for more
    than one directory at once returns nothing.
    
    If it does then it retries each one individually.
    
    This can potentially have a false positive if the user has multiple
    empty directories which are queried at once. The consequence of this
    will be that ListR is disabled for a while until the directories are
    found to be actually empty in which case it will be re-enabled.

Yes its fine now, it automatically disables ListR to avoid giving incorrect results
is this fastlist disabling check done globally for other rclone commands that accept fast list flag too ? because if lets say someone is doing rclone copy from remote where fastlist is bugged and he explicitly uses fast list flag , it will skip files while cloning

> Yes its fine now, it automatically disables ListR to avoid giving incorrect results

Great!

> is this fastlist disabling check done globally for other rclone commands that accept fast list flag too ? because if lets say someone is doing rclone copy from remote where fastlist is bugged and he explicitly uses fast list flag , it will skip files while cloning

Yes it will. `ListR` is the internal command that `--fast-list` uses so it will cover all cases. Some commands like `rclone size` use `ListR` without the `--fast-list` flag because it doesn't use any more memory.

I've merged this to master now which means it will be in [the latest beta](https://beta.rclone.org) in 15-30 mins and released in v1.52.1

issue.title: drive: prevent retries when query filter returned no entries

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
#### What is the purpose of this change?

This patch fixes retries caused by optimization introduced by
- #5023

The `driveFs.ListR` result handler `listRRunner` treated empty directory listings returned by Google Drive in response to query constrained by `--min-age` and/or `--max-age` as an indication of the Google bug and retried the listing request with `--fast-list` turned off resulting in overall degraded performance.

There are two possible solutions for that:
1. disable query filter optimization in presence of `--fast-list` i.e. call ` SetUseFilter(ctx,false)` in `listRRunner()` to reset the optimization flag.
2. treat empty directory listings as an acceptable result if the query optimization was applied (ignoring possible server bugs)

This PR applies the latter solution, which bears risk of hitting the drive empty result bug
but it can provide better overall performance.

#### Was the change discussed in an issue or in the forum before?

https://forum.rclone.org/t/performance-degradation-between-v1-56-2-and-v1-57-0-when-copying-to-google-drive-using-max-age-min-age-and-fast-list/27580/2
